subject: Tyska 3
title: Konjunktiv II: politeness and hypotheticals
sourceSummary: The basics of Konjunktiv II — polite wishes and requests, plus simple hypothetical sentences with "hätte gern" and "würde + infinitive".

questions.prompt: Choose the most polite phrasing: "I would like a coffee."
questions.opener: A common polite phrase using the Konjunktiv II of haben.
questions.explanation: "Ich hätte gern..." (Konjunktiv II of haben + gern) is the standard polite phrase for ordering or wishing for something, corresponding to "I would like" in English. "Ich will" sounds too blunt/childish in this situation.

questions.prompt: Which Konjunktiv II form belongs to "können"?
questions.opener: The form is usually built from the simple-past stem plus an umlaut.
questions.explanation: The Konjunktiv II of irregular verbs is often formed by adding an umlaut to the simple-past stem: "können" → simple past "konnte" → Konjunktiv II "könnte".

questions.prompt: Choose the most polite question: "Could you help me?"
questions.opener: Compare it with the plain present-tense question "Können Sie...?".
questions.explanation: "Könnten Sie...?" (Konjunktiv II) is more polite and softer than the plain present-tense question "Können Sie...?", roughly like the difference between "can you" and "could you" in English. "Konnten" (without the umlaut) is the simple past, not the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Which construction is used for most verbs to express something hypothetical ("would do")?
questions.opener: Only a handful of common verbs have their own short Konjunktiv II forms.
questions.explanation: For most verbs, the hypothetical "would" form is built with conjugated "würde" + infinitive at the end of the clause: "ich würde gehen" (I would go). Only a few common verbs (sein, haben, the modal verbs) have their own short Konjunktiv II forms (wäre, hätte, könnte), which are preferred over the würde construction.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence: "If I had time, I would read more."
questions.opener: Both halves of a hypothetical conditional sentence use Konjunktiv II.
choices: Wenn ich Zeit hätte, würde ich mehr lesen.
Wenn ich Zeit habe, würde ich mehr lesen.
Wenn ich Zeit hätte, ich würde mehr lesen.
Wenn ich hätte Zeit, würde ich mehr lesen.
questions.explanation: Both halves of a hypothetical conditional sentence use Konjunktiv II: the "wenn" clause ("hätte", verb at the end) and the main clause ("würde ich mehr lesen", with inverted word order since the wenn-clause occupies position one).

questions.prompt: What does "ich möchte" (Konjunktiv II of mögen) mean?
questions.opener: It differs from the present-tense form "ich mag".
questions.explanation: "Ich möchte" is the polite equivalent of "I would like", while the present-tense form "ich mag" means "I like/enjoy".

questions.prompt: Rewrite the sentence more politely using Konjunktiv II: "Ich will noch eine Frage stellen." (I want to ask one more question.)
questions.opener: Which Konjunktiv II form belongs to the "wollen" family and is used as its polite equivalent?
questions.answer: Ich möchte noch eine Frage stellen.
steps: "Will" (present tense of wollen) sounds blunt and a bit brusque in a polite context, e.g. in a lesson or when addressing someone you don't know.
The Konjunktiv II of "mögen" is "möchte", the standard polite equivalent of "will".
"Will" → "möchte": "Ich möchte noch eine Frage stellen." — softer and more polite, roughly "I would like to ask one more question".

questions.prompt: What is Konjunktiv II, when is it used, and what forms does it take?
questions.opener: Politeness and hypotheticals — two main uses.
questions.answer: Konjunktiv II expresses polite wishes/requests and hypothetical/unreal situations (corresponds to "would" in English). Common short forms (preferred over würde): sein → wäre, haben → hätte, werden → würde, können → könnte, müssen → müsste, dürfen → dürfte, mögen → möchte. For most other verbs: conjugated würde + infinitive at the end, e.g. "ich würde fahren". Polite phrases: "Ich hätte gern..." (I would like), "Könnten Sie...?" (could you...?), "Ich möchte..." (I would like). Hypothetical sentences: wenn-clause in Konjunktiv II + main clause in Konjunktiv II, e.g. "Wenn ich Geld hätte, würde ich reisen." (If I had money, I would travel.)
